## Proof

**Yes**, such sequences exist.

We use the fact that Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a Radon measure, hence both inner and outer regular: for every measurable set $A$ with $\mu(A)<\infty$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a compact $K\subset A$ with $\mu(A\setminus K)<\varepsilon$, and an open $G\supset A$ with $\mu(G\setminus A)<\varepsilon$.

**Decomposition.** Write $\mathbb{R}^n=\bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty} Q_j$ as a disjoint union of half-open unit cubes, and set $E_j=E\cap Q_j$. Then $\mu(E_j)<\infty$ and $E=\bigcup_j E_j$ (disjoint).

**Outer approximation.** For each $j,m$, by outer regularity pick open $G_{j,m}\supset E_j$ with
$$\mu(G_{j,m}\setminus E_j)<\frac{1}{m\cdot 2^{j+1}}.$$
Set $G_m=\bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty}G_{j,m}$; this is open and $E\subset G_m$. Then
$$\mu(G_m\setminus E)\le\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\mu(G_{j,m}\setminus E_j)<\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{m\cdot 2^{j+1}}=\frac{1}{m}.$$
Since $E\subset\bigcap_m G_m$, we have $(\bigcap_m G_m)\setminus E\subset G_m\setminus E$ for every $m$, so
$$\mu\!\Big(\big(\bigcap_m G_m\big)\setminus E\Big)\le\mu(G_m\setminus E)<\frac1m\to 0.$$
Hence $\mu\big((\bigcap_m G_m)\setminus E\big)=0$.

**Inner approximation.** For each $j,m$, by inner regularity pick compact $K_{j,m}\subset E_j$ with
$$\mu(E_j\setminus K_{j,m})<\frac1m.$$
Set $K_m=\bigcup_{j=1}^{m}K_{j,m}$, a finite union of compact sets, hence compact, with $K_m\subset E$.

Fix $j$. For every $m\ge j$ we have $K_{j,m}\subset K_m$, so
$$E_j\setminus\Big(\bigcup_m K_m\Big)\subset E_j\setminus K_{j,m}\quad(m\ge j),$$
giving $\mu\big(E_j\setminus\bigcup_m K_m\big)\le\mu(E_j\setminus K_{j,m})<\frac1m\to 0$. Thus $\mu\big(E_j\setminus\bigcup_m K_m\big)=0$ for each $j$.

Now
$$E\setminus\Big(\bigcup_m K_m\Big)=\bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty}\Big(E_j\setminus\bigcup_m K_m\Big),$$
a countable union of null sets, so $\mu\big(E\setminus\bigcup_m K_m\big)=0$.

**Combining.** We have $K_m\subset E\subset G_m$ for all $m$, with $\bigcup_m K_m\subset E\subset\bigcap_m G_m$. Therefore
$$\Big(\bigcap_m G_m\Big)\setminus\Big(\bigcup_m K_m\Big)=\Big[\big(\bigcap_m G_m\big)\setminus E\Big]\;\sqcup\;\Big[E\setminus\big(\bigcup_m K_m\big)\Big],$$
a disjoint union of two null sets. Hence
$$\mu\!\Big(\big(\bigcap_m G_m\big)\setminus\big(\bigcup_m K_m\big)\Big)=0.$$
